High-level answers up front:
- BYOK: supported on Dedicated (BYOK via customer KMS integration / HSM-backed keys). Hosted supports customer-supplied keys via a Bring-Your-Own-Key integration (CMEK) for organizations on enterprise Private plans.
- HSM: We use HSM-backed key storage (FIPS validated HSMs) for KEKs in production where CMEK is configured.
- Key escrow: Redwood does not operate a general-purpose key escrow. For enterprise customers that require escrow for regulatory reasons we can arrange a mutually agreed third-party escrow process under contract; otherwise our DR model uses encrypted backups with customer KEK wrap/unwrap procedures and a documented emergency key recovery runbook.
- Rotation cadence: DEKs are rotated automatically per workload (default 30 days) and KEKs are rotated per policy (default 12 months) unless the customer configures a stricter cadence.
- In-transit: TLS 1.2+ (TLS 1.3 preferred) with restricted ciphers; mutual TLS is optional and commonly required for Dedicated/private installs.
- Cross-region replication: When using provider multi-region KMS (CMEK MRKs) keys are replicated via the cloud provider's MRK feature. For customer-managed on-prem HSMs we offer a documented replication pattern but do not directly replicate customer HSMs for them.

Sarah / team — digging into the details below and attaching our custody matrix and a machine-readable rotation log for the range you asked about. Short technical clarifications:

In-transit:
- All external client traffic (hosted API and Dedicated ingress) requires TLS 1.2+; TLS 1.3 is negotiated where supported. We enforce strong AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM/ChaCha20-Poly1305).
- Control plane channels (token management, admin APIs) use mTLS internally between services. For Dedicated/private installs we support customer-configured mTLS for control plane endpoints.

At-rest:
- Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256-GCM data encryption keys (DEKs). DEKs are generated per-tenant/per-service and are wrapped with a KEK held in an HSM-backed KMS.
- KEKs are HSM-protected (FIPS 140-2 validated HSMs in cloud providers or customer-managed HSMs in Dedicated). Where customers use their own HSM, KEK material never leaves the HSM.

Key lifecycle and rotation:
- DEKs: rotated automatically on default 30-day cadence; customers can configure shorter intervals for higher security workloads.
- KEKs (master/wrapping keys): default rotation 12 months; emergency rotation can be performed at any time.
- Last KEK rotation for the production KEK used in the hosted eu-west-1 cluster was 2028-02-17 (UTC).
- Rotation and key usage events are written to an immutable audit stream, exported to our secure bucket with object versioning and retention policies; we can provide signed export slices for audit.

Key escrow / recovery:
- Redwood does not retain plaintext customer key material. For escrow requirements we support contract-level arrangements with third-party escrow vendors; we are happy to introduce our legal/security teams to set that up.
- Disaster recovery relies on wrapped key backups and a documented recoverability test plan that we can share under NDA.

Attached: key_custody_matrix_2028-05-11.xlsx (matrix of who holds what), rotation_events_2028-05-01_to_2028-05-10.csv (CSV)

If you want formal attestation wording I can produce a short signed PDF attestation that says: "Redwood Inference uses HSM-backed KEKs, data encrypted with AES-256-GCM, and enforces TLS 1.2+/1.3 in transit; master key rotation cadence is 12 months default; DEKs rotate by default every 30 days unless configured otherwise."
